summary:
The §3.3 UI survey is written. Everything it plans is still to be built: nothing of Phase 3 is implemented, and I neither built nor ran the player.

The player already has the pieces of §3.3, but separately. Two per-frame VMAF views run off the in-player analyzer, which records no PTS. The network sidebar's Alignment tab has a timeline that already zooms with the wheel, pans by dragging and fits on double-click. There is also a GL time ruler for manifest tags, and a seek bar with its scrub pipeline.

The plan is a new ImGui panel docked above the control stack. It loads a mirage_vmaf report and matches it to the open master (by SHA-256, else by URL) and to the variant on screen. It draws one curve per variant on the reference's timeline as per-column min/max envelopes, so short dips stay visible, with event lanes and detected drops. A click picks the lowest frame near the cursor, shows its attribution and seeks through the existing s_seek_to entry point. The math (view, envelope, hit testing, loading, matching, time mapping, seek decision) goes in ImGui-free files tested in mirage_tests, since mirage_tests links no ImGui (D-031). By my reading none of the recommended changes touches the render or decode path; section 3 lists the ones that would.

One measurement changes the picture. A small library-API program (not the player) seeks two synthetic HLS playlists the way Demuxer.cpp does. With FFmpeg 8.1.1's hls demuxer, frames of an ad whose timestamps restart at an EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY cannot be reached by any seek. Clicking a low point inside such an ad therefore cannot seek to that frame without a decode-path change (D-007). That is a difference from the work order the owner needs to decide on, together with how D-069's synthetic ad is timestamped.

Other agents are writing into the same survey directory; I did not touch their files. I deleted the FFmpeg and Khronos sources I had downloaded, since the directory may be committed; the documents cite them by URL. The worktree is unchanged (git status clean at 75cf6e0).
key_findings: Measured (experiments/hls-seek-probe/run-output.txt, FFmpeg 8.1.1, libavformat 62.12.101): when timestamps continue across EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY, a seek by PTS lands at the start of the right segment (11.0/12.5/14.5 -> 10.000/12.000/14.000).

Measured, same run: with an ad whose PTS restart (0.040-2.000 between content at 10.000-11.960 and 12.000-13.960), no seek reaches the ad. By its PTS (0.5) av_seek_frame fails, and the player's clamp (Demuxer.cpp:487-495, reproduced in the probe) sends it to the stream's start (10.000). By playlist position (12.5) the ad is skipped and the seek lands at 12.000. Content after the ad by PTS (13.0) lands at 12.000; by playlist position (14.5) it reaches end of file.

The probe's results follow from hls.c n8.1.1: segments are found by first_timestamp plus EXTINF sums (L1916-1944, L2551-2554, L2667-2760), packets with DTS below that position are dropped (L2565-2586), and AVFMT_NOGENSEARCH makes a failed read_seek final (hls.c L2852, seek.c L622-638).

The report's per-frame ref_pts/dis_pts are raw best-effort PTS in seconds (VMAFAnalyzer.cpp:280-285, 731-734; tools/mirage_vmaf.cpp:158 sets record_pts), the same form as the player's last_pts (main.cpp:1617-1625). The in-player analyzer records none: it passes default options (VMAFAnalyzer.h:169-173; VMAFAnalyzer.cpp:819, 872).

Both existing curves average the frames of each pixel column, so a dip narrower than a column flattens (PlayerUI.cpp:1542-1552; DebugHUD.cpp:1061-1077). Their position marker picks frame pos_frac x N with pos_frac = last_pts / duration (PlayerUI.cpp:1557-1569; main.cpp:3173-3174), which assumes frames spread evenly from PTS 0.

By reading: the tag ruler's click-to-seek never fires. s_click_x/y are cleared at main.cpp:2824-2825 before the ruler reads them at 2918-2919 in the same iteration, and events are pumped only at the end of the loop (3501-3519).

By reading: tag times are playlist time, an EXTINF sum from 0 (ManifestParser.cpp:236, 340-343), but the ruler draws them on the seek bar's raw-PTS [0, duration] scale (UiWidgets.cpp:135-138), so its ticks sit off by the stream's start time. Also #EXT-X-CUE-OUT-CONT is taken as a cue-out (ManifestParser.cpp:320) and #EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35 is dropped (328-338).

Input capture: ImGui sets WantCaptureKeyboard while keyboard navigation is active (imgui.cpp:5128-5137, 13045, v1.91.9), and on_key then returns early (main.cpp:241-242). NetInspector works around this by dropping focus (NetInspector.cpp:387-394). The 'VMAF Analysis' window does neither (PlayerUI.cpp:1411), so by reading a click in it can leave the shortcuts dead. A panel overlapping the ##controls window would take the seek bar's hover and clicks (PlayerUI.cpp:35-39, 585-588; imgui.cpp:5123). Seeks must go out once per click release and never while scrubbing (the 'buzz on one note' guard, main.cpp:3333-3339).

Drawing many points: AddPolyline reserves up to 4 vertices per point under 16-bit indices, and PrimReserve does not split a single primitive (imgui_draw.cpp:680-686, 795-797; imgui.h:266). One call must therefore stay at or below 16384 points.

HiDPI: the GL HUD widens lines with glLineWidth(scale) (DebugHUD.cpp:346, 633) in a forward-compatible core context (main.cpp:820-823), where only width 1 is guaranteed (Khronos glLineWidth page). The bottom stack also mixes units: kStripPx is not scaled (ThumbnailStrip.h:123-124; main.cpp:2779).

Matching: ManifestParser drops an EXT-X-STREAM-INF entry when a blank or comment line separates it from its URI (ManifestParser.cpp:254, 281), while VMAFLadder allows that (VMAFLadder.h:15-18). The two resolve URLs differently (ManifestParser.cpp:180-189 vs VMAFLadder.h:116-123). So entries can be matched by index only after the master's SHA-256 matches and the entries are checked.

The Alignment tab's timeline is the pattern to reuse: wheel zoom about the cursor by 0.8/1.25 clamped to [0.5 s, 1.5 x extent + 1 s], drag to pan, double-click to fit, click = release that moved less than 3 px (NetInspectorAlign.cpp:637-662). Its helpers sit in an anonymous namespace (69-107), so they cannot be unit-tested today.
ScrubBar is initialised (main.cpp:875-880) but never drawn anywhere in src/.
open_issues: For the owner (D4): clicking a low point inside an ad whose timestamps restart cannot seek to that frame with FFmpeg 8.1.1's hls demuxer. This is a difference from the work order. The agent recommends saying so in the panel and offering the segment before the discontinuity; a 'play to frame, then pause' request or a Demuxer change would each need a D-007 plan.
For the owner (D5): whether D-069's synthetic ad continues or restarts its timestamps. It decides whether acceptance test (2)'s cue point can be clicked to; the agent recommends making both ladders.
The single time axis for streams whose PTS restart at a discontinuity (D3): (sequence, PTS), playlist time, or continuous PTS. This belongs to §3.1's model.
Seek cases not measured: a discontinuity whose timestamps jump forward, fMP4 segments, and a master with several variants (the player opens the master, possibly a deduplicated copy).
Unverified: whether the player's PTS through the master equal mirage_vmaf's through each media playlist.

Owner choices listed in ui.md 2.6: placement (D1), JSON reader written in the repo vs a new dependency (D2), the toggle key (D8), whether prefs.txt counts as the config file the work order requires (D9), playlist segment tables in the report (D11).
MEASUREMENT PENDING: report size, load time and memory for real ladders, and the cost of building the min/max pyramid.
Findings by reading still to confirm with a player run: F1 (the tag ruler's dead click), F2 (its tick offset), F6 (the VMAF window's keyboard focus).
Whether recording the player's own variant switches as a D-068 session log counts as touching the render path: it only observes, but the code sits in the present step.
The new QA flags proposed in ui.md (--timeline, --ui-timeline, --timeline-report) and a 'keep the media' switch for D-069's generators do not exist yet; the scripted QA run needs them.
Other agents are writing into the same survey directory (e.g. testgen/, schema.md). The probe's result on restarted ad timestamps is relevant to the test-generation and schema surveys.
